name: Sorted – Post & Taxonomy Reorder
author: Galaxy Weblinks

sections.description:
Sorted – Post & Taxonomy Reorder gives you full control over the order of your WordPress content.
You can reorder posts, pages, and any custom post types or taxonomies effortlessly through an intuitive drag-and-drop interface.
Perfect for customizing the display order on your site without writing a single line of code.

Once activated, a “Reorder” menu will automatically appear under each post type in the WordPress admin area. From there, simply drag and drop your items to set the desired order. The plugin supports all registered post types and taxonomies, making it a lightweight and powerful content-sorting solution for any website.

Key Features:

  • Drag-and-drop interface to reorder posts and taxonomies.
  • Supports all post types (posts, pages, custom post types).
  • Reorder categories, tags, and custom taxonomies
  • Simple one-click activation, no configuration needed
  • Automatically integrates with existing admin menus
  • Lightweight and developer-friendly

Here’s a link to the documentation for the plugin. This will help you learn more about its features and how to use it.
Documentation

For any feedback or queries regarding this plugin, please contact our Support team.
sections.installation:
This plugin can be installed directly from your site.
1. Log in and navigate to Plugins → Add New.
2. Type “Sorted – Post & Taxonomy Reorder” into the Search and hit Enter.
3. Locate the Sorted – Post & Taxonomy Reorder plugin in the list of search results and click install now.
4. Once installed, click the Activate link.

It can also be installed manually.

  1. Download the Sorted – Post & Taxonomy Reorder plugin from WordPress.org.
  2. Unzip the package and move it to your plugin’s directory.
  3. Log into WordPress and navigate to the Plugins screen.
  4. Locate Sorted – Post & Taxonomy Reorder in the list and click the Activate link.
sections.faq:
How do I use the Sorted – Post & Taxonomy Reorder plugin?

After activating the plugin, go to the WordPress dashboard. You’ll find a “Reorder” submenu under each post type. Simply drag and drop your items to reorder them.

Does it work with custom post types and taxonomies?

Yes! The plugin supports all registered custom post types and taxonomies by default. No additional setup is required.

Will it affect my front-end display?

Yes, if your theme or query uses the default WordPress order (menu_order or orderby => ‘menu_order’). Most custom queries will automatically respect the order you set using this plugin.
